analysis.title: Catch Up Or Catch Down: Goldman Says Either Way, Momentum Loses As Breadth Sits At Dot-Com Extremes
key_insights: Goldman's Ben Snider (US Weekly Kickstart) says rising cost of capital has caused the equity market to downgrade growth expectations. The Cyclicals vs. Defensives pair fell 6% in two weeks, and a sharp cut in investor positioning amplified the moves.
The S&P 500 is 2% below its record high, but the median S&P 500 stock is 15% below its own high. Goldman's preferred breadth measure is near its narrowest level since the Dot-Com Bubble.

Goldman says narrow breadth can resolve through a 'catch down' by recent outperformers or a 'catch up' by laggards. Either outcome reverses the Momentum factor, so Snider advises caution on Momentum despite the historical growth-cycle playbook.

The 10Y yield fell more than 20bp in two weeks after rising more than 100bp over six months. USD high yield spreads widened more than 20bp, with the stress concentrated in AI-related issuers while Energy and Utility credits held up.
GS neoclouds basket (GSXUNEOC) fell 24.8% on the week and semis fell eight straight sessions, the longest streak since May 2006. The GS high-momentum pair (GSPRHIMO) fell 14.5%.

Prime Services data show US long/short net leverage fell 3.2 points to 43.7%, a 0th-percentile reading on a five-year lookback and the largest weekly drop since Liberation Day. Info Tech saw the largest percentage net selling on Goldman's Prime record, which goes back to 2016.
Goldman's baseline is S&P 500 EPS growth of 36% in 2026 slowing to 11% in 2027, or 18% adjusted for non-recurring accounting distortions. The same adjustment lowers 2026 growth to 29%.
Goldman estimates AI capex contributes roughly half of S&P 500 EPS growth now. The contribution fades into 2027 as capex growth slows and depreciation rises, and turns negative by 2028.
Goldman's 2028 EPS estimate of $460 is 7% below the $492 bottom-up consensus.

Early Q3 read, with 10% of the index reported: 53% of companies beat consensus by more than one standard deviation. That is above the 25-year average of 50% but below the 64% average of the past four quarters. Revision breadth is positive but fading.

Since 1985, quarters of positive but decelerating real growth delivered a median S&P return of 3% with the P/E slipping 1%. Momentum has historically been the best factor in this regime, at a 1.8pp median quarterly long/short return.

Momentum fell 8% this week and slid from roughly 130 to around 120 on Goldman's index (approximate, read off a chart). Since June the Russell 2000 is down 10% and the GS Neoclouds basket is down 44%, while the S&P 500 ex-AI (SPXXAI) rallied 4%.
Worst weekly S&P performers were AI hardware names: COHR -26%, LITE, HPE and FLEX -25% each, SMCI -24%, DELL -23%. Best were FICO +16%, CTSH +12% and several insurance brokers.

Catch-up basket: consumer-facing laggards. Goldman economists expect lower energy prices and rates in 2027 to lift real income growth, especially for the bottom income quintile. Hedge fund Consumer Discretionary exposure is at multi-year lows, and the GS low-income consumer discretionary basket (GSXULOWD) is up 7% since the start of October.

Catch-down basket: 23 defensive Health Care and Consumer Staples names from the Russell 1000 with low realized volatility, high FCF yield and high FCF conversion. The list's median trailing FCF yield is 6% vs 4% for the Russell 1000, and realized volatility is 29 vs 36.

Hedge funds net bought US Health Care at the fastest pace in seven months this week. Health Care, Comm Services and Staples were the only global sectors net bought, and Health Care was the best S&P sector of the week at +5.3%.
Goldman keeps its year-end S&P 500 target of 8,000 (3% upside from 7,744) and 8,700 at 12 months. Snider wants clients long the catch-up basket, hedged with the catch-down basket, and short Momentum.

The ZeroHedge author leans toward the catch-down. The catch-up case needs oil to fall nearly 30%, the Fed to stay on hold after a hot September CPI print, and low-income consumers to replace hyperscaler capex. META and TSLA report Wednesday, with 14% of S&P market cap reporting next week.
